sections.heading: What a word analogy is
sections.body:
A **word analogy** shows two pairs of words that are linked in the same way. The link between two words is called their **relationship**.

It is written like this: **PEN : WRITE :: KNIFE : CUT**

- The single colon ( : ) means **"is to"**.
- The double colon ( :: ) means **"as"**.
- Read it as: "Pen is to write as knife is to cut."

On the exam you will see two kinds of item:

1. **Fill the blank:** PEN : WRITE :: KNIFE : ___. You choose one word.
2. **Find the pair:** "Which pair has the same relationship as PEN : WRITE?" You choose a pair, such as knife : cut.

Both kinds test the same skill: seeing exactly how the first two words are linked.

sections.heading: The bridge sentence method
sections.body:
A **bridge sentence** is a short sentence that states exactly how the first two words are linked. You then test every choice in it.

1. **Make the bridge** from the first pair: "A pen is used to write."
2. **Put each choice into the same sentence:** "A knife is used to cut." True. "A knife is used to kitchen." Makes no sense.
3. **Keep the one choice that makes a true sentence.**

Tips:

- **Keep the order.** If the stem puts the tool first, the answer must also put the tool first.
- **Make the bridge exact.** "A carpenter works with a hammer" is loose, because a carpenter also works with a helper. "A carpenter uses a hammer as a work tool" is exact.
- **If two choices fit, make the bridge more exact** and test again.
- **Test all four choices.** Don't stop at the first one that looks related.

sections.heading: Relationships of meaning and parts
sections.body:
A **synonym** is a word with the same meaning as another word. An **antonym** is a word with the opposite meaning.

| Relationship | Bridge sentence | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same meaning | A means the same as B | big : large |
| Opposite meaning | A is the opposite of B | early : late |
| Part to whole | A is one part of B | door : house |
| Whole to part | A is made up of many B | week : day |
| Member to group | A is one member of B | player : team |

For parts and wholes, always check which comes first: the smaller part or the bigger whole.

sections.heading: Relationships of use, kind, cause and degree
sections.body:
A **category** is a group of things of the same kind, like fruit or vehicle. A **cause** makes something happen, and the **effect** is the result. **Degree** means how strong or weak something is.

| Relationship | Bridge sentence | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tool and action | A is used to B | pen : write |
| Tool and what it measures | A is used to measure B | ruler : length |
| Worker and tool | A uses B as a work tool | barber : scissors |
| Worker and workplace | A works in a B | nurse : hospital |
| Kind and category | A is a kind of B | tilapia : fish |
| Category and kind | A is the group, and B is one kind of it | fruit : banana |
| Cause and effect | A can cause B | typhoon : flood |
| Degree | A is a mild form of B | big : huge |

sections.heading: Common traps
sections.body:
- **Reversed order.** LEAF : TREE is part to whole. TREE : LEAF is whole to part. A choice with the right link in the wrong order is wrong.
- **Related, but a different link.** A knife is linked to kitchen, bread and cut, but only "cut" fits "is used to". Being related is not enough. The link must be the same.
- **Degree is not the same meaning.** Big and huge are not exact synonyms, because huge is much bigger.
- **Nearly opposite is not opposite.** Warm is not the opposite of hot. Cold is.
- **A sign is not a kind.** A frown shows anger, but a frown is not a kind of anger.
- **A loose bridge.** If more than one choice fits, your bridge is too loose. Make it more exact and test again.

glossaryTerms.definition: A word analogy shows two pairs of words that are linked in the same way, like PEN : WRITE :: KNIFE : CUT.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Analogy – paghahambing ng dalawang pares ng salita na pareho ang ugnayan

glossaryTerms.definition: A relationship is the way two words are linked, such as "means the same as" or "is one part of".
glossaryTerms.taglish: Relationship – ang ugnayan o koneksyon ng dalawang salita

glossaryTerms.definition: A bridge sentence is a short sentence that states exactly how the first two words are linked. You test each choice in it.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Bridge sentence – maikling pangungusap na nag-uugnay sa dalawang salita; dito mo susubukan ang bawat choice

glossaryTerms.definition: A synonym is a word that means the same, or nearly the same, as another word.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Synonym – salitang magkasingkahulugan, gaya ng big at large

glossaryTerms.definition: An antonym is a word that means the opposite of another word.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Antonym – salitang magkasalungat ang kahulugan, gaya ng early at late

glossaryTerms.definition: A category is a group of things of the same kind, like fruit, fish or vehicle.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Category – grupo o uri na kinabibilangan ng isang bagay

glossaryTerms.definition: A cause makes something happen. The effect is what happens as a result.
glossaryTerms.taglish: Cause and effect – sanhi at bunga

glossaryTerms.definition: Degree is how strong or weak something is, like big (mild) and huge (strong).
glossaryTerms.taglish: Degree – tindi o lakas; halimbawa, malaki kumpara sa napakalaki
